title: 1960 AHSME Problem 24
statement: If \(\log_{2x}216=x,\) where \(x\) is real, then \(x\) is:

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: a non-square, non-cube, non-integral rational number

solutions.text:
The equation is equivalent to \[ (2x)^x=216. \] Since \(216=6^3,\) \(x=3\) satisfies the equation. To see it is the only admissible real solution, note that the base requires \(x>0\) and \(2x\ne1;\) on \(0\lt x\lt\frac{1}{2},\) \(x\ln(2x)\lt0,\) while for \(x>\frac{1}{2}\) the function \(x\ln(2x)\) is strictly increasing. Thus \(x=3,\) a non-square, non-cube integer.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Use \(216=6^3\) to recognize a real solution
